name: Annan Perumal Temple, Thiruvellakkulam (Annan Koil)
deity: Vishnu as Srinivasa, called Annan Perumal, with Alarmelmangai Thayar (utsavar Padmavathi) and a separate shrine of Kumudavalli Nachiyar — Thiruvellakkulam, the "Tirupati of the Thirunangur group"
period: A Divya Desam of Chola Nadu, one of the eleven Thirunangur shrines, sung by Thirumangai Alvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
summary: At Annan Koil near Sirkazhi, Srinivasa is worshipped as Annan Perumal, the elder brother of the Lord of Tirumala — a Divya Desam of Chola Nadu where Thirumangai Alvar sang ten verses and met Kumudavalli.

sections.history: Thiruvellakkulam, known today as Annan Koil, is one of the 108 Divya Desams and belongs to Chola Nadu. It is one of the eleven Vishnu shrines of Thirunangur near Sirkazhi. Its Lord is Srinivasa Perumal, called Annan Perumal, the elder brother of Thiruvenkatamudaiyan of Tirumala; pilgrims who cannot reach Tirupati have long held a visit here to be equal to it. Thirumangai Alvar devoted ten verses to the shrine, Periya Thirumozhi 4.7, and tradition says he addressed only two Perumals as 'Anna' — this Lord and the Lord of Tirupati. The architecture is classed as Chola, and the most recent consecration took place in October 2016. The hymns place its attestation in the eighth century.
sections.architecture: The sanctum is crowned by the Tattvadyotaka vimana, and the temple belongs to the Chola architectural tradition, renewed at its latest kumbhabhishekam in October 2016. Alarmelmangai Thayar has her own shrine, and Kumudavalli Nachiyar is honoured in a separate shrine as well. The temple tank, from which the shrine takes its name, is the Swetha Pushkarini, the 'white tank' — Vellai Kulam in Tamil.
sections.legends: Two stories gather here. Tradition tells of Prince Swetan, foretold to die young, who on the sage Vasishtha's advice chanted the Mrityunjaya mantra for a month under a vilva tree beside the tank and was granted long life; the Swetha Pushkarini bears his name. The second is Kumudavalli's: a celestial maiden who came to the tank for kumuda flowers is said to have stayed on earth. The chieftain Neelan, who became Thirumangai Alvar, sought her hand, and she asked him to embrace the Vaishnava way and serve devotees — the turning point of his life.
sections.festivals: The Thirunangur Garuda Sevai is held in the Tamil month of Thai, the day after Thai Amavasai, when the utsavars of the eleven shrines gather at Thirumanimadam. Festivals of Thirumangai Alvar, whose story is woven into this shrine, are kept with devotion. The temple is a popular place to pray for long life and health. Confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: A quiet village temple that pilgrims treat as a Tirupati nearer at hand. Offer prayers at the Lord's shrine, then at Kumudavalli's, and walk to the white tank where the story of Swetan is told. Many come here to pray for long life and good health. It makes an unhurried stop among the eleven Thirunangur Divya Desams.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; the Thai Garuda Sevai is the busiest day. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Annan Koil lies a short distance east of Sirkazhi in Mayiladuthurai district, in the Thirunangur group on the road towards Thiruvenkadu. Sirkazhi has a railway station on the Chennai–Chidambaram–Mayiladuthurai line; the major airports are Tiruchirappalli and Chennai. Take a taxi or autorickshaw from Sirkazhi, since the eleven shrines lie close together.
